A SINGLE model wears the shop's garment and chats with the viewer in Thai, the way a friendly seller would. Each clip exists to SELL that garment: reveal the complete outfit, the fit and the way it moves, the fabric and the details, plus the back whenever the style permits. The opening 2 seconds must hook the viewer (full outfit plus a hook line).
Strict rules: the garment has to match the product photos exactly — never redesign it, change its colour or simplify it; one and the same model with an unchanged look across every scene; most scenes show the full body (head to toe); nobody else appears; no brand names and no logos; never make up prices, discounts, stock levels or sizes that the user did not supply; the "outfit" text must stay word-for-word the same in every clip; preserve the model's true body size (never make her slimmer); never liken her to a celebrity; never refer to body size in the title or caption.
SPOKEN LINES (vo): Thai only, 4-6 words in each 2-second scene, no scene left empty, flowing as a single continuous friendly talk: scene 1 carries the hook, next come fabric / cut / how it feels, then size and fit drawn only from the user's data, and the final scene ends on a call-to-action (e.g. กดตะกร้าได้เลย). Write every number out in Thai words; do not use English abbreviations; use "ตัวนี้" where a brand name would go; never let a line end with "...".

fsStylePlan.mirror: MIRROR SELFIE — the entire clip is a SINGLE unbroken take with zero cuts. Holding a smartphone, the model faces a full-length mirror and we watch her reflection head-to-toe, just like a genuine seller's OOTD video. All movement stays small and natural: shifting her weight, rotating the body to the left and right (max ~45°) so the side silhouette shows, smoothing the fabric, touching a detail, a hand on the hip, a single small step back. She keeps speaking to her reflection from start to finish. camN = nothing beyond slight framing drift, never a fresh angle. When the selected location lacks a mirror, add a full-length standing mirror to it.
fsStylePlan.walk: WALK TO CAMERA — filmed as ONE continuous shot with the camera locked at chest height (a slightly low, heroic angle). In scene 1 the model starts a few metres back and comes toward the lens with relaxed, self-assured strides (NOT a runway catwalk), her clothes moving on every step. Next she eases off, halts at a medium-full distance, strikes a pose (hand resting on hip, a touch of the hair, a slight turn sideways) and speaks to the camera. Her whole body stays in frame in every scene.
fsStylePlan.spin: TURN AROUND — shot as ONE continuous take on a static camera, framing the full body from head to toe. Scene 1 shows her from the front while she delivers the hook line. Next she rotates slowly in place (roughly 3 seconds for one complete turn), letting viewers see both sides and the BACK of the look, the hem flaring slightly, before she faces the lens once more and speaks. Strictly ONE slow complete turn in each 10 seconds — never spin fast or twirl.
fsStylePlan.lookbook: LOOKBOOK SHOOT — a photographer behind the camera captures her (third-person view, NOT a selfie, NO mirror, NO phone held). Each scene (2 s) hard cuts to a fresh pose: full-body contrapposto, a hand placed on the hip, a single step ahead, a glance over the shoulder (showing the outfit's back), and a medium shot on a single detail (neckline, sleeve, waist). Most scenes frame the full body; the last scene comes back to a full-body pose. Her speech runs on through the cuts as a single voice.
fsStylePlan.minimal: MINIMAL TONE AD — styled after a high-end, minimalist product commercial: a tidy, uncluttered set kept within ONE colour family that matches the garment (a soft pastel or neutral backdrop, no more than one plain plinth or prop), lit softly and evenly. The camera is third-person (NOT a selfie, NO mirror, NO phone). Each scene (2 s) hard cuts: a calm, graceful full-body pose, a slow push-in, a medium shot of the fabric or a detail, an unhurried turn to the side, then a full-body pose to close. Speech is calm and premium.
fsStylePlan.live: LIVE SELLING — ONE continuous take that looks like a TikTok Shop livestream viewed through the seller's own phone: the camera IS the viewer's eyes (static, at chest height) — NO tripod, phone or camera may appear in the frame. Framed waist-up toward the lens (conversational distance, NOT full body), the model chats warmly in the manner of a live seller, tugs the fabric and stretches it out toward the lens so its texture shows, moves back until the whole outfit is in view, then steps in close again to deliver the call-to-action. No cuts.
fsStylePlan.hanger: HANGER TO WORN — scene 1: only the garment, hung on a wooden hanger in front of a plain wall (nobody in shot; her voice comes from off-screen). Next, hard cut to the model dressed in that same garment, changing pose with each 2-second scene: full-body from the front, from the side, a detail of the fabric, the back seen over the shoulder, and a closing full-body pose. Camera is third-person — no selfie, no mirror.
fsStylePlan.street: STREET SNAP — ONE continuous hand-held take, as if a friend walking beside her is recording on a phone (third-person, NOT a selfie, NO mirror, she holds no phone). She wanders at an easy pace, throws a look back over her shoulder, laughs, fixes her bag or her hair, then turns toward the lens and speaks as though chatting to a friend. The hand-held camera follows softly and naturally, keeping the full body in frame most of the time.
fsStylePlan.unbox: UNBOX TO WORN — scene 1: seated or standing at a table, the model opens a shipping box and raises the folded garment out of it toward the camera, speaking with excitement (what she holds must match the garment photos). Next, hard cut to her dressed in it, switching pose with each 2-second scene: full-body from the front, from the side, a detail of the fabric, the back seen over the shoulder, and a closing full-body pose. Camera is third-person — no selfie, no mirror.
fsStylePlan.breeze: CINEMATIC BREEZE — a dreamlike fashion commercial with a filmic feel: gentle backlight or golden-hour sun, a light breeze stirring the fabric and her hair in each shot, and a slow gliding camera. The camera is third-person (NOT a selfie, NO mirror, NO phone). Each scene (2 s) hard cuts: a full-body pose as the hem moves, an unhurried turn to the side, a medium shot of the fabric caught in the wind, a look back over the shoulder, then a full-body pose to close. Her speech keeps a normal pace, calm and warm.
fsStylePlan.fabric: FABRIC CLOSE-UP — scene 1: an extreme macro of the fabric on her body (weave, texture, stitching, a button or lace edge) while her hand brushes or gently stretches it; scene 2: another detail close-up (seam, neckline finish, cuff or hem). Then hard cuts that pull back: a medium shot showing how the fabric drapes and moves, then full-body poses wearing it; the final scene is a full-body pose. Third-person camera, no selfie, no mirror. Her talk explains the fabric (feel, thickness, stretch, breathability) only from the user's data.
fsStylePlan.mix3: ONE PIECE, 3 LOOKS — the shop's garment stays exactly the same in every scene; only simple add-ons change to make 3 looks: look 1 simple and casual, look 2 smart (an open blazer or cardigan, neat shoes), look 3 going-out (a small bag, a bold accessory or a hat). Split the scenes evenly into the 3 looks with a hard cut between looks; each look has at least one full-body pose. Add-ons never cover or change the main garment, are plain and have no logos. Third-person camera, no mirror. Her talk names each look in Thai (e.g. ลุคแรก ลุคทำงาน ลุคออกเที่ยว).
fsStylePlan.transition: OUTFIT TRANSITION — scene 1 (0-2 s) only: the model in plain grey loungewear (a simple oversized T-shirt and shorts — NOT the shop's garment) faces the camera, says the hook and claps her hands at the end of the scene. Scene 2 starts with an instant jump-cut: same spot, same framing, she now wears the shop's garment, hair and look neatly styled. From scene 2 on, a new pose every scene: full-body front, side, a fabric detail, back over the shoulder, a full-body pose at the end. Third-person camera, no mirror. The loungewear appears in scene 1 only; every other scene shows the exact shop garment.

fsOccasionPlan.work: โอกาสที่ใส่: ไปทำงาน — ท่าและฉากดูเรียบร้อยน่าเชื่อถือ (เช่น ออฟฟิศ ร้านกาแฟใกล้ที่ทำงาน) พูดถึงการใส่ทำงานทั้งวัน ใส่เข้าประชุม
fsOccasionPlan.travel: โอกาสที่ใส่: ไปเที่ยว — ท่าสบาย ๆ ถ่ายรูปสวย ฉากเที่ยว (เช่น ริมทะเล ถนนในเมือง ตึกแถวเก่า) พูดถึงการใส่เที่ยว เดินทาง ถ่ายรูปขึ้น
fsOccasionPlan.date: โอกาสที่ใส่: ไปคาเฟ่หรือเดต — ท่าน่ารักละมุน ฉากคาเฟ่หรือถนนไฟยามค่ำ พูดถึงลุคไปเดต ถ่ายรูปในคาเฟ่
fsOccasionPlan.event: โอกาสที่ใส่: ไปงานหรือออกงาน — ท่าสง่า ดูโดดเด่น ฉากโรงแรมหรือสตูดิโอ พูดถึงใส่ไปงานแต่ง ปาร์ตี้ งานเลี้ยง
fsOccasionPlan.home: โอกาสที่ใส่: อยู่บ้านสบาย ๆ — ท่าผ่อนคลาย ฉากห้องนอนหรือห้องนั่งเล่น พูดถึงความสบาย ขยับง่าย ใส่ได้ทั้งวัน

fsTonePlan.lux: โทนการขาย: หรูดูแพง — พูดน้อย ประโยคสั้น นุ่มและมั่นใจ เน้นคุณภาพ เนื้อผ้า งานตัด ไม่เร่ง ไม่ตะโกน ไม่ใช้คำว่าถูก
fsTonePlan.fun: โทนการขาย: ขายแบบมีมุก — มีมุกเบา ๆ หรือเปรียบเทียบขำ ๆ 1-2 จุด (ไม่ล้อรูปร่าง ไม่หยาบ) แต่ยังขายของชัด ปิดด้วยชวนกดตะกร้า
fsTonePlan.rush: โทนการขาย: เร่งปิดการขาย — กระชับ เร็ว ชวนสั่งเลยตั้งแต่กลางคลิป ถ้ามีโปรให้พูดโปรตั้งแต่ต้น ห้ามแต่งเรื่องของใกล้หมด สต็อก หรือเวลาจำกัดเองถ้าผู้ใช้ไม่ได้ให้ข้อมูล
